about: One entry per rule. The lint reads profile, requires, gating, title and fix from here; Test-Rulebook.ps1 proves every bad example triggers its rule and every good example stays clean; New-RuleDocs.ps1 generates RULES.md and agent-rules.md from it.

features.toolkit: Uno Toolkit (UnoFeatures Toolkit, Uno.Toolkit* package, using:Uno.Toolkit.UI)
features.themes: An Uno.Themes theme (UnoFeatures Material, Cupertino or Simple*, Uno.Themes/Uno.Material packages)

rules.title: Border with CornerRadius + fill/stroke/padding -> CardContentControl
rules.why: A hand-drawn card ignores the theme's card styles and states, so every card in the app drifts a little differently.

examples.bad:
<Border CornerRadius="{StaticResource Radius200CornerRadius}" Background="{ThemeResource SurfaceBrush}">
  <StackPanel><TextBlock Text="Order 1042" /><TextBlock Text="3 items" /></StackPanel>
</Border>

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: image clips and one-child badges in uno.chefs were false positives, now exempt.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint still flags image clips and badges (lab fixture corpus-card).

rules.title: hex literal outside the palette override -> theme brush
rules.why: A literal colour does not follow light/dark or a brand change; the theme's palette is the one place colours belong.

fix.default: a theme brush ({ThemeResource ...Brush}) from the app's theme, or a colour defined once in the theme's colour override file. A literal colour does not follow light/dark or brand changes.
fix.material: a Material role brush (PrimaryBrush, OnSurfaceBrush, SurfaceContainerHighBrush, OutlineVariantBrush, ErrorBrush...). The only colours an app defines live in its ColorPaletteOverride file; brand colour goes there. Status and chart colours map to Primary/Secondary/Tertiary/Error and their containers.

enforcement.runtime: Switch light/dark with the App MCP and check the element's colour changes.

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: theme seed colours, fully transparent #00 colours and ThemeDictionaries colours (recommended) were false positives, now exempt.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint also flags named colours (Fill="Red"), which the lab misses (244 hits in uno.toolkit.ui samples). uno-lint flags transparent colours and MAUI XAML.

rules.title: colour literal in C# -> theme resource + redraw on theme change
rules.why: Colours chosen in code skip the theme entirely and never change with light/dark.

fix.default: read the colour from theme resources (a Brush dependency property bound with {ThemeResource ...Brush}, or a lookup keyed on ActualTheme) and redraw on ActualThemeChanged.

enforcement.runtime: Switch light/dark and check drawn colours change.

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: C# Markup ColorPaletteOverride.cs, Theme.Colors keys and dependency property defaults were false positives, now exempt.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint reports these under HEX (UNOL001), so an 'allow cscolor' comment does not suppress them there. uno-lint flags dependency property defaults and MAUI C#.

rules.title: margin/padding/spacing literal -> Uno.Themes Space* token
rules.why: Literal spacing cannot be rescaled from the theme and drifts between screens.

fix.default: Uno.Themes Space* tokens: {StaticResource Space400Thickness} for Margin/Padding, {StaticResource Space200} for Spacing. Rescale the whole app with DefaultSpacing on the theme.

rules.evidence: Opinionated: uno.chefs (reference app) has 193 literal spacings, so this stays strict-only.

rules.title: corner radius literal -> Uno.Themes Radius* token
rules.why: Literal radii cannot be rescaled from the theme and drift between controls.

fix.default: Uno.Themes Radius* tokens: {StaticResource Radius200CornerRadius}. Rescale with DefaultCornerRadius on the theme.

rules.evidence: Opinionated: uno.chefs has 52 literal radii, so this stays strict-only.

rules.title: app brush with one value for both themes -> theme brush, ThemeDictionaries, or *Invariant name
rules.why: A brush defined once outside ThemeDictionaries keeps its light-mode value in dark mode.

fix.default: use a theme role brush; else define the key per theme in ThemeDictionaries; name it *Invariant/*OnDark/*OnLight/*Fixed only when its ground is fixed in both themes.

examples.good:
<Page.Resources>
  <ResourceDictionary>
    <ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries>
      <ResourceDictionary x:Key="Light"><SolidColorBrush x:Key="AccentBrush" Color="{StaticResource BrandColor}" /></ResourceDictionary>
      <ResourceDictionary x:Key="Dark"><SolidColorBrush x:Key="AccentBrush" Color="{StaticResource BrandColorDark}" /></ResourceDictionary>
    </ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries>
  </ResourceDictionary>
</Page.Resources>

enforcement.runtime: Switch light/dark and check the brush changes.

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: lightweight styling in one control's Resources, StaticResource aliases and converters keyed *Brush were false positives, now exempt.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint does not flag a brush whose Color is a {ThemeResource}; the lab does. Unverified which is right at runtime. uno-lint flags converters keyed *Brush.

rules.title: hand-built back button -> utu:NavigationBar
rules.why: A hand-built back button misses the platform back gesture and the shared app bar layout.

fix.default: utu:NavigationBar with a MainCommand AppBarButton; back navigation and the Android back gesture come with it.

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: Navigation.Request="-" closing a ContentDialog in uno.chefs was a false positive, now exempt.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint flags the ContentDialog close button.

rules.title: event handler or Visibility toggle in code-behind -> commands, visual states, bindings
rules.why: Logic in code-behind cannot be tested and spreads: one workaround gets copied to every page.

fix.default: commands on the model (ICommand), VisualStateManager states driven by model state, or Visibility bound to the model.
fix.toolkit: utu:CommandExtensions.Command, commands on the model, utu:VisualStateManagerExtensions.States bound to model state, or Visibility bound to the model.

rules.evidence: dotnet new unoapp (blank) wires Frame.NavigationFailed in App.xaml.cs: app-level wiring, exempt. uno.chefs keeps 2 handlers (flyout opening, map tap) as deliberate glue; strict-only.

rules.title: overlay/sheet toggled in code-behind -> flyout, dialog or !Route
rules.why: Hand-toggled overlays miss focus handling, dismissal and back navigation.

fix.default: a Flyout or ContentDialog, or Visibility bound to model state; filter state lives in the model.
fix.navigation: uen:Navigation.Request="!Route" to a Page (opens as a flyout) with a DrawerFlyoutPresenter style; filter state lives in the model.

rules.evidence: Rare in the corpus (1 hit in uno.themes).

rules.notes: AdaptiveTrigger hits run only with Uno Toolkit and cannot be suppressed; code-behind width checks run in every project.
rules.title: AdaptiveTrigger or code-behind breakpoint -> utu:Responsive / utu:ResponsiveView
rules.why: Two breakpoint systems in one app drift apart; width logic in code-behind cannot be previewed or tested.

fix.default: move the breakpoint into XAML: a VisualStateManager state with an AdaptiveTrigger (or add Uno Toolkit and use {utu:Responsive}). Never compare widths in code-behind or keep width flags on a view model.
fix.toolkit: breakpoints are always {utu:Responsive} in XAML for a value, utu:ResponsiveView when the whole template changes (custom thresholds via a utu:ResponsiveLayout resource). No WinUI AdaptiveTrigger (not suppressible), never code-behind, never width flags on a view model.

enforcement.build: BannedApiAnalyzers: P:Microsoft.UI.Xaml.AdaptiveTrigger.MinWindowWidth and MinWindowHeight in BannedSymbols.txt + WarningsAsErrors RS0030. Proven 2026-11-17 on Uno.Sdk 6.7.30 desktop; banning the type false-positives via BindableMetadata.g.cs.
enforcement.runtime: Resize to Narrow and Wide with the App MCP and compare the visual tree.

rules.evidence: A private Toolkit app had 6 AdaptiveTriggers across 3 pages. uno.gallery has 31.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint UNOL005 only checks code-behind and its fix text suggests AdaptiveTrigger. Policy question.

rules.title: custom control shadowing a platform/Toolkit control
rules.why: A re-implemented control misses the theme, accessibility and fixes the shipped one gets.

fix.default: use the platform/Toolkit control named above with lightweight styling before writing a custom control; then Windows Community Toolkit 8.x.

rules.evidence: Uno.Samples: BusyIndicator -> ProgressRing is a true positive.

rules.title: inline or shape-built icon geometry -> icon font or keyed set data in Icons.xaml
rules.why: Hand-drawn icons drift in size and stroke and cannot be swapped as a set.

fix.default: SymbolIcon/FontIcon on the Fluent symbol font, or keyed path data from one open icon set (Material Symbols, Fluent System Icons) in Icons.xaml via PathIcon Data="{StaticResource ...}". Never hand-draw icons. Illustrations get "xaml-lint: allow icon - illustration".

rules.evidence: uno.gallery's 88 hits are showcase pages that draw paths on purpose.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint suppression covers one element; the lab covers the element under the comment and its children.

rules.title: platform branch in a model/view model -> platform service or Platforms/ partial
rules.why: Platform branches in models make them untestable on other targets and scatter platform logic.

fix.default: move the branch into a platform service (interface in shared code, implementation per head or in a Platforms/ partial) and inject it; models stay platform-neutral.

rules.title: blocking .Wait()/.Result/GetResult() -> await
rules.why: Blocking on a task freezes the UI thread and can deadlock.

fix.default: await the task. If the caller cannot be async (constructor, property), start the load from a command or MVUX feed instead of blocking.

enforcement.build: Microsoft.VisualStudio.Threading.Analyzers VSTHRD002 covers synchronous waits; not yet tested on an Uno Platform project.

rules.evidence: Corpus 2026-11-17: .Result after a completion check (uno.ch9) and mock endpoints (uno.chefs) were false positives, now exempt.

rules.title: {Binding State.Value, Mode=TwoWay} on an input in an MVUX model -> {Binding State}
rules.why: The MVUX bindable proxy already exposes the state's value; a two-way binding to .Value on an input does not write back.

fix.default: bind the state itself on a two-way input: {Binding State, Mode=TwoWay}. The MVUX proxy already exposes the value. Inside a FeedView template bind {Binding Data.X}.

enforcement.runtime: Type into the field with the App MCP and read the model state back. Not yet run: the narrowed claim is unverified.

rules.evidence: Uno Platform's own MVUX samples (MvuxHowTos, ToDo, Commerce, uno.chefs) bind .Value for Navigation.Data, CommandParameter, DataContext, converters, ItemsSource and IsEnabled; narrowed to TwoWay input bindings.
rules.differsFromUnoLint: uno-lint flags every .Value binding: 9 hits in uno.chefs, 12 in Uno.Samples, all in working official code.

rules.title: info: x:Bind with no Mode outside item templates (OneTime default)
rules.why: x:Bind defaults to OneTime, so a value that changes later never shows.

fix.default: x:Bind is OneTime by default: add Mode=OneWay for values that change, or a comment saying OneTime is intended.

rules.evidence: Info only: getter-only computed properties are OneTime by design.
